# SQL translation report

Each ported model's compiled source SQL (Trino, [AML-Compliance-Platform](https://github.com/hatimelguebbass/AML-Compliance-Platform) at `db07483041d7`) was transpiled to Databricks SQL by sqlglot 30.31.0, run on the dev SQL warehouse (Databricks SQL 2026.44), and its rows compared with the table the reviewed port built, lineage columns aside. Measured by `make translation`.

| Outcome | Models |
|---|---|
| identical | 9 of 13 |
| different | 1 of 13 |
| fails | 3 of 13 |
| untranslated | 0 of 13 |

Outcomes: `identical` gives the port's rows; `different` runs with other rows; `fails` is rejected by the warehouse; `untranslated` is rejected by sqlglot. The seven AML rules are ephemeral models inlined into `gold.aml_alert_transfer` and measured with it.

## Hand changes

Reviewed in `migration/translation.yaml`.

Applied to every model:

- **engine**: Dated models replace their business date with Delta REPLACE WHERE (dbt strategy replace_where), not a delete pre-hook then an append, and are not partitioned. One atomic commit per date instead of two, so a failed run never leaves a date half deleted. Delta does not need partitions at this size; clustering is measured in step 8.
- **syntax**: Load time written as convert_timezone('UTC', current_timestamp()). The source wrote UTC wall-clock time without zone with AT TIME ZONE, which Databricks SQL does not have.
- **types**: Contract types in Spark names (string, timestamp_ntz for timestamp(6), timestamp for timestamp(6) with time zone, array<T>). dbt compares the declared types with the warehouse's.
- **engine**: Columns tagged with their classification, pseudonym columns masked, tables created with their full column definition. Unity Catalog policy of ADR 0005, checked against the classification by `lakemig assess`.

`silver.customer_history`:

- **boundary**: Birth year read as delivered instead of year(birth_date). The birth date never crosses the boundary; the export reduces it to its year (ADR 0003).
- **boundary**: Change batches read from bronze.change_batch. The source's audit.change_batch crosses as one more delivered table.
- **semantics**: Dates of capture and update instants taken in UTC with convert_timezone. A cast of a TIMESTAMP to DATE uses the session time zone on Databricks; Trino used the zone of the value, UTC. Identical on a UTC session, wrong by a day around midnight on another.
- **types**: Years cast to bigint. year() returns int on Databricks and bigint on Trino; the contract keeps the source's type.

`silver.account_history`:

- **boundary**: Change batches read from bronze.change_batch. The source's audit.change_batch crosses as one more delivered table.
- **semantics**: Dates of capture and update instants taken in UTC with convert_timezone. As for silver.customer_history.

`silver.card_history`:

- **boundary**: Change batches read from bronze.change_batch. The source's audit.change_batch crosses as one more delivered table.
- **semantics**: Dates of capture and update instants taken in UTC with convert_timezone. As for silver.customer_history.

`silver.party`:

- **syntax**: array_agg(customer_id order by customer_id) written array_sort(array_agg(customer_id)). Databricks SQL has no ORDER BY inside array_agg. sqlglot translates it to collect_list and drops the ordering: its rows matched on the measured run only because of execution order, which Spark does not guarantee.

`silver.payment_transfer`:

- None.

`silver.card_transaction`:

- None.

`silver.fx_rate`:

- None.

`gold.aml_alert_transfer`:

- **syntax**: Alert id written md5(text) instead of lower(to_hex(md5(to_utf8(text)))). Databricks md5 hashes the UTF-8 bytes and returns lower-case hex, the same id.
- **semantics**: Volume spike average cast to decimal(38, 2). Trino divides decimal(38,2) by an integer at scale 2, rounding half up; Databricks keeps scale 6. A threshold compared with an average at another scale flips boundary cases.

`gold.aml_alert`:

- **types**: Credited and debited sums cast to decimal(38, 2). Databricks sums decimal(22,2) to decimal(32,2), Trino to decimal(38,2); the contract keeps the source's type.

`gold.aml_rule`:

- None.

`observability.dataset_profile`:

- **types**: Bins cast to string instead of varchar. Spark has no unbounded varchar; a string is what the source's varchar was.

`observability.volume_check`:

- **semantics**: Median positions computed with div instead of /. Trino's / on two integers is an integer division; Spark's returns a fraction, and element_at with a fractional position fails. Same positions, same median.
- **syntax**: Ratio written case when ... end instead of the two-argument if. Spark's if takes exactly three arguments; Trino's returns null without the third.
- **syntax**: Baseline counts gathered with collect_list instead of array_agg. Both are sorted by array_sort before the median is read, so the order of gathering does not matter.
- **semantics**: Weekend recognized by dayofweek in (1, 7) instead of day_of_week in (6, 7). Spark numbers days from Sunday (1) to Saturday (7), Trino from Monday (1) to Sunday (7). sqlglot rewrites day_of_week(d) as (dayofweek(d) % 7) + 1, which numbers Saturday 1 and Friday 7: Thursdays and Fridays become the weekend and every baseline changes.

`observability.distribution_drift`:

- **semantics**: Weekend recognized by dayofweek in (1, 7) instead of day_of_week in (6, 7). As for observability.volume_check.
